1. Validate the current bill: confirm the meter reads imply 787 kWh (62,473 − 61,686) and that the line items sum to $147.84; any mismatch becomes billing_error_usd with billing_error_suspected = true.

2. Assign each billing period to the OpenEI tariff(s) by date. Last month (2026-02-24 to 2026-03-26) falls entirely under the pre-2026-04-10 tariff; the current bill (2026-03-26 to 2026-04-25) straddles the 2026-04-10 tariff change, so prorate the fixed charge and blend the per-kWh rate across the boundary.

3. Set days_usd = 0 because both periods are 30 days.

4. Estimate weather_usd using the NOAA degree-day history: compare last month (2.5 CDD / 549.5 HDD) to the current period (57 CDD / 226 HDD), derive the weather-driven kWh difference from the historical kWh vs. CDD/HDD relationship, and value that difference in dollars.

5. Compute price_usd from the tariff rate changes applied to a baseline usage, then set usage_usd as the residual so that price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals the observed change of −$8.60.

6. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd (null if no error is suspected).
